cards.title: Addressing Russian Seniors
cards.body: Russian military culture emphasizes hierarchy. Address superiors by their rank and last name. Civilians prefer titles like 'Gospodin' (Mr) or 'Gospozha' (Mrs) with their last name.
doThis: Use full rank and last name for military personnel
Use formal titles with last names for civilians
avoidThis: Informal language with those senior to you

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Russia (2025)

cards.title: Navigating Checkpoints in Russia
cards.body: Checkpoints are common. Carry identification and base passes at all times. Be polite and patient. Expect thorough searches and questions about your purpose.
doThis: Always carry ID and base passes
Remain polite and patient

cards.title: Respecting Rank in Russia
cards.body: In Russia, hierarchy is important. Use formal titles and last names for seniors unless invited to do otherwise. Be polite and patient during conversations.
doThis: Address seniors as 'Gosnodyn' (Mr.) or 'Gospozha' (Ms.) followed by their last name
Wait for seniors to initiate informal address
Show patience and attentiveness during conversations
avoidThis: Interrupting or disagreeing openly with seniors

cards.title: Navigating Refusals and Criticism
cards.body: Russians may indirectly refuse or criticize to save face. Pay attention to tone and context. Avoid public disagreement or harsh criticism.
doThis: Listen for indirect refusals like 'We'll see' or 'It's difficult'
Give and accept criticism privately and gently
Maintain a calm and respectful tone
avoidThis: Raising your voice or showing frustration

cards.title: Respecting Hierarchy in Refusal
cards.body: Russian military culture values hierarchy. When refusing an order or request, address superiors with respect and provide a valid reason. Avoid direct refusal; instead, offer alternatives or seek guidance.
doThis: Use formal titles and patronymics when addressing seniors
Provide a clear, respectful reason for refusal
Offer alternative solutions or seek advice

cards.title: Respect Hierarchy in Russia
cards.body: Russian culture values hierarchy and respect for seniors. Address superiors with their first name and patronymic (father's name with a suffix). Maintain formality in communication to save face and show respect.
doThis: Use formal greetings like 'Zdrastvuyte' for strangers and seniors.
Address seniors with their first name and patronymic.
Maintain a respectful and formal tone in conversations.
avoidThis: Avoid using first names only with seniors.
Avoid informal language or slang with superiors.
Avoid interrupting or contradicting seniors publicly.

cards.title: Save Face in Russia
cards.body: Russians value saving face and may seem blunt. Criticism should be constructive and private. Disagreements should be handled diplomatically to maintain harmony and respect.
doThis: Offer criticism privately and constructively.
Use diplomatic language in disagreements.
Avoid public criticism or embarrassment.
avoidThis: Avoid blunt or direct criticism in public.
Avoid interrupting or talking over others.
Avoid sensitive topics like politics or historical events.

cards.title: Respect Hierarchy in Meetings
cards.body: Russian workplaces are hierarchical. Wait for seniors to initiate conversations. Address them using their rank and last name. Avoid interrupting or disagreeing openly. Punctuality is valued, so be on time.
doThis: Address seniors by rank and last name
Wait for seniors to initiate conversations
Be punctual for meetings

cards.title: Navigate Checkpoints Politely
cards.body: Checkpoints are common. Have your ID and base pass ready. Greet security staff politely. Avoid sudden movements. If refused entry, stay calm and ask for a senior officer.
doThis: Have ID and base pass ready
Greet security staff politely
Ask for a senior officer if refused entry

cards.title: Respecting Hierarchy and Titles
cards.body: Russian air force personnel value rank and formal addresses. Use titles and last names with seniors. Women hold some senior positions but face barriers in the highest ranks.
doThis: Address seniors with their rank and last name
Use formal titles (e.g., 'Colonel Ivanov')
avoidThis: Assume senior roles are held by men

cards.title: Navigating Checkpoints and Security
cards.body: Security staff may be strict. Be patient and cooperative. Women may face additional scrutiny due to traditional gender roles.
doThis: Carry identification at all times
Follow instructions calmly and respectfully

cards.title: Respect Orthodox Hierarchy
cards.body: The Russian Orthodox Church holds significant cultural importance. Show respect to religious leaders and understand their influence. Avoid public criticism of the church or its practices.
doThis: Address religious leaders with respect, such as 'Father' for priests.
Acknowledge the cultural significance of the ROC.
avoidThis: Disrespect religious leaders or their teachings.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Russia (2025)

cards.title: Navigating Religious Sensitivity
cards.body: Avoid discussing proselytization or criticizing traditional religions. Be mindful of the restrictions on religious activities and the government's control over religious organizations.
doThis: Respect the boundaries set by the government on religious activities.
Avoid discussing proselytization or criticizing traditional religions.
avoidThis: Engage in religious debates that could be seen as disrespectful.
Criticize the government's control over religious organizations.

cards.title: Gift Giving: Hierarchy and Respect
cards.body: Russians value hierarchy. Gifts show respect to seniors. Present gifts with both hands. Avoid expensive gifts to superiors. Gifts are usually opened when received. Common gifts include chocolates, flowers, or souvenirs from your home country.
doThis: Address seniors with their title and last name.
Present gifts with both hands.
Choose thoughtful, modest gifts.
avoidThis: Use first names with seniors unless invited.

source.doc: AFCLC Expeditionary Culture Field Guide: Russia (2025)

cards.title: Gift Giving: Saving Face and Etiquette
cards.body: Russians value politeness and saving face. Gifts are usually refused once or twice before acceptance. Present gifts discreetly. Avoid giving even-numbered flowers, which are for funerals. Yellow flowers can symbolize infidelity.
doThis: Expect initial refusal; persist politely.
Present gifts discreetly.
Choose odd-numbered flowers.
avoidThis: Insist too strongly on first refusal.

cards.title: Respecting Rank at Meals
cards.body: Rank is important in Russia. Seniors are addressed formally and served first. Wait for seniors to start eating and follow their lead.

Wait for seniors to begin eating
Follow seniors' lead on meal pacing
avoidThis: Disagree openly with seniors about food choices

cards.title: Addressing Russian Air Force Seniors
cards.body: In Russia's air force, hierarchy is important. Use formal titles and patronymics (father's name + 'ovich'/'ovna') when addressing seniors. Maintain a respectful tone and avoid familiarity unless invited.
doThis: Use 'Gospodin' (Mr.) or 'Gospozha' (Mrs.) with the last name for foreigners.
Address seniors with their first name, patronymic, and last name.
avoidThis: Use first names or nicknames with seniors unless invited.

cards.title: Radio Etiquette with Russian Personnel
cards.body: Russian communication is direct and concise. On the radio, be clear and to the point. Avoid small talk and maintain a professional tone. Use 'Zdrastvuyte' (Hello) and 'Dobriy den' (Good day) for formal greetings.
doThis: Speak clearly and concisely.
Use formal greetings like 'Zdrastvuyte'.
avoidThis: Engage in small talk or informal conversation.

cards.title: Addressing Russian Superiors
cards.body: In Russia's air force, hierarchy is crucial. Address seniors by their rank and last name. Avoid familiarity unless invited. Criticism should be constructive and private. Disagree respectfully, focusing on facts.
doThis: Use formal titles and last names for seniors
Give criticism privately and constructively
Disagree respectfully with factual evidence

cards.title: Navigating Checkpoints and Security
cards.body: Checkpoints are common. Carry identification and follow instructions. Be polite to security staff and local nationals. Refusal is often implied, not direct. 'No' might be signaled by silence or evasion.

Be polite to security staff and locals
Look for implied refusals
